explain.say: A sycamore or maple seed has a heavy seed at one end and a thin papery wing at the other. When it breaks off the tree, the heavy end falls first.

explain.say: As the wing sweeps round, it makes a tiny whirlwind of low pressure along its front edge. This swirl sucks the wing upward, giving extra lift, so the seed falls slowly at a steady speed.

explain.say: Falling slowly gives the wind more time to carry the seed sideways, often tens of metres from its parent tree, where it has more room and light to grow.

faq.q: Why does a sycamore seed spin?
faq.a: Its wing is slanted and weighted at one end. As it falls, the air pushes unevenly on the slanted wing, which turns the seed round and round, a motion called autorotation.
asks: What makes a helicopter seed twirl?

faq.q: How does spinning slow the seed down?
faq.a: Each sweep of the spinning wing creates a small whirlwind along its front edge. The low pressure inside it pulls up on the wing, giving extra lift, so the seed falls much more slowly.
asks: How do helicopter seeds stay up?

faq.q: Why do trees want their seeds to travel?
faq.a: A seed that lands right under its parent has to compete with it for light, water and space. Seeds carried further away have a better chance of growing.
asks: Why do seeds need to spread out?

faq.q: How fast does a sycamore seed fall?
faq.a: A spinning maple or sycamore seed falls at only about 1 metre per second, much more slowly than the same seed would without its wing.
asks: How slowly do helicopter seeds fall?

faq.a: Yes. Engineers have built tiny sensors and drones shaped like spinning seeds that drift gently down, and helicopters use autorotation to land safely if their engine fails.
asks: What can we learn from helicopter seeds?

facts: Maple and sycamore seeds stay aloft using a swirl of air on their wing's front edge, called a leading-edge vortex, as shown in a 2009 study in the journal Science.
A spinning maple seed falls at roughly 1 metre per second.

quiz.why: The spinning wing makes lift, slowing the fall, which gives the wind time to carry the seed away from its parent tree.

wrong.1: The seed lands gently; spinning slows it rather than driving it in.
wrong.2: Spinning is about falling slowly, not about birds.
